newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan says Islamists' support growing.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan says Islamists' support growing.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday that support for his Islamist Welfare Party was growing despite military-led pressure for a crackdown on religious activism.
"The injustices carried out against Welfare are opening the way for our people to run to Welfare," Erbakan told deputies at a party meeting.
Welfare says it has three million members, which makes it by far the largest party in Turkey. It won 21 percent of the vote in 1995 elections, giving it the highest number of deputies in parliament.
Welfare's reluctance to go along with anti-Islamist demands from the National Security Council is threatening the future of its 10-month-old coalition with conservatives.

Erbakan's Islamists have in particular expressed strong opposition to a demand that state education be extended to an eight-year, uninterrupted period, which they see as a threat to the influence of Islamist schools.
Two ministers from the conservative wing of the coalition resigned last month in frustration at the efforts by Welfare to resist the army's demands.
